stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

When the power went out, the employees save their files and turned off the computers.
hints: Look at all the verbs in the sentence. Do they all show the same time?
"Went out" and "turned off" are both in the past tense. Is every verb in the past?
Rule: keep the tense consistent (the same) when the actions happen at the same time. Find the verb that breaks the pattern.

solution.methodName: Find the time clue, then match the verb

steps.action: Find the time clue: "When the power went out". It is in the past, so the whole event is finished.
"Turned off" is also in the past and matches. "Save" is in the present tense, so it does not match.
steps.why: The employees saved their files at the same time they turned off the computers, so both verbs must be in the past.

steps.action: The error is "save their files". It should be "saved their files".

trapNotes.went out: "Went" is the past form of "go", so "went out" is correct. It sets the time of the whole sentence: the past.
trapNotes.turned off the computers: Some choose this because it does not match "save". But "turned off" agrees with "went out". It is "save" that breaks the pattern.
trapNotes.No error: "Save" may look fine because "employees" is plural. It agrees in number, but it is in the wrong tense. The sentence is about the past.
